title: Autotune: default batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching and KV-caching, introduces quantization profile registry and CLI, and wires unit-economics tooling into the Console. No breaking changes to public API.
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token unit cost for common production workloads by providing sane, workload-aware defaults and tooling for: request batching, prefix/KV caching defaults, quantization profiles for vetted model variants, and basic unit-economics visibility in the Console. This PR implements an end-to-end feature set: 1) runtime autotune defaults that pick batching and cache/window settings based on historical request traces and SLO targets; 2) a quantization profile registry with curated profiles (8-bit, mixed-precision candidates) and a developer CLI to evaluate quality vs. cost; 3) a lightweight unit-economics export and Console panel that surfaces per-route cost estimates and recommendations. Changes are feature-flagged behind `cost_autotune_v1` and `quant_profiles_v1` for staged rollout. Checklist: - [x] Implement batching/caching defaults + runtime hooks - [x] Add quantization profile registry and CLI tooling - [x] Add unit-econ export endpoint and Console panel wiring - [x] Integration tests for autoscaling/backpressure interactions - [x] Perf regression tests against stable benchmark suite - [x] Docs and migration notes Testing & validation: Unit and integration tests included. Perf canary ran against perf-canary cluster (see commit notes). A/B rollout planned: enable for 10% of traffic for 48h then scale to 100% if no quality regressions detected. See linked Linear items for evaluation plan and rollout criteria.
